source_text: Ut intellegatur ab unoquoque motu propriae voluntatis attractum; et iam non fecunditas seminum, sed studiorum pravitas arguetur. Ceterum si illud unum originale voluisset intellegi, non utique in sequentibus peccata multa dixisset, quae per gratiam dimissa testatur.
pass_a_gloss: So that it may be understood as drawn by each one by a motion of proper will; and now not the fecundity of seeds, but the crookedness of pursuits will be accused. But if he had wanted that one to be understood as original, he would certainly not in the following have said many sins, which he testifies have been dismissed through grace.

lemmas.lexica: LS fecunditas; Blaise blessed fertility of marriage
LS semen; Blaise bodily seed vs transmitted sin
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: It should therefore be understood as acquired by each person through the movement of his own will. What is accused will then be not the fertility of seed, but the perversity of deliberate conduct. If, however, he had intended that one sin to be understood as original, he certainly would not afterward have spoken of many sins which, as he testifies, are forgiven through grace.

choices.why: God-blessed fertility of the first pair; Julian will not let Paul accuse it.
Bodily seed of generation; Julian denies it carries a will's sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
